### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0df241eea55a099005206bd3245ac0633074852b` — the merge of head `297278a90c063e195105a880ac85ec0d30845ecf` into base `767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0df241eea55a099005206bd3245ac0633074852b && git checkout 0df241eea55a099005206bd3245ac0633074852b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb 297278a90c063e195105a880ac85ec0d30845ecf && git checkout -B drift-repro 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb && git merge --no-ff 297278a90c063e195105a880ac85ec0d30845ecf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `297278a90c063e195105a880ac85ec0d30845ecf`
Local-runs: none

Face: `declaration` (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`). There is no path-derived face: the diff is `packages/services/service-analytics` only, plus a changeset.

Inputs: card #32373 with every comment, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (3 files, +173/−4), and the check-runs on this head (37 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`AnalyticsServicePluginOptions.narrowObjectReadAdmission?(objectName, context)` is a new public option on an exported type. This is a widening of the public surface. Right.**
  - It composes over the provider the plugin always wires: the host's `admitObjectRead`, or else the security bridge. Read in `plugin.ts`: the bridge answers in every resolution state, so `base` is never undefined.
  - It is asked only when `base` admits, and it admits only on exactly `true`. So the composition can refuse more and never admit more. A malformed answer refuses.
- **Refusal envelopes are unchanged and come from the existing gate.** `false`, or any answer other than `true`, gives `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403. A throw from either side propagates, so the gate answers `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503, fail-closed. **Right.**
- **Without the option the wiring is the same provider reference.** No behaviour moves for an existing host. **Right.**
- **Edge read:** with no security service and no host provider, the bridge's `absent` arm admits (and warns once, as before), and the narrowing then decides alone. This tightens nothing that was already refused and opens nothing. **Right.**
- **Not exported:** `composeNarrowedReadAdmission` is module-private.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. A non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). `Check Changeset` is green on this head. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Rejected alternative:** the dev rejected a `decorateReadAdmission(base)` hook because it could widen. **Agreed.**
- **Cloud follow-up:** dropping the by-name decoration of the private `readAdmissionProvider` in `security-enterprise` belongs to the cloud seat. It is noted on the card's carrier, outside this repository.
- **Deviation:** the dev did not re-run the package suite on the final head after the last `main` merge, which touches no `service-analytics` file. CI on this head is green. **Accepted.**

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32373-analytics-read-admission-option`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w`

**VERDICT: PASS**
